https://www.politico.eu/article/slovenia.text: Slovenia’s parliament on Wednesday allowed prosecutors to pursue a criminal case against former Prime Minister Robert Golob over allegations that he improperly meddled in police staffing after taking office in 2022. All 75 lawmakers present — including Golob himself — voted against granting him parliamentary immunity, allowing proceedings to move forward. The decision was taken without debate or explanations of the voting. Golob had already told parliament he would not invoke immunity and wanted the case resolved as quickly as possible. Advertisement Advertisement The corruption case stems from allegations by Golob’s former Interior Minister Tatjana Bobnar, who said he pressured her to make personnel changes inside the police. Bobnar resigned in December 2022 and subsequently reported the alleged pressure to prosecutors and Slovenia’s anti-corruption commission. Golob has denied wrongdoing. Ljubljana’s District Court opened a judicial investigation in October 2025. Prosecutors had to ask parliament to lift Golob’s immunity after he was elected as an MP this year. Golob’s liberal Freedom Movement remains Slovenia’s largest opposition party .

Boutrous pointed out that the three letters – to CNN, Politico and MS NOW – were unsigned and not on White House letterhead. All three cited articles published by the outlets months ago, most of them written by reporters who do not have passes to the White House. The letters, Boutrous said, looked a “post hoc” attempt to justify the bans that the president himself told reporters on Friday were in response to overly negative coverage of his performance as president, by grafting on national security grounds. https://www.politico.eu/article/greens-t.text: STRASBOURG — The Greens in the European Parliament chose Terry Reintke and Nicu Ștefănuță as their new leadership team on Tuesday, promising an energetic, campaign-focused push to revive a political group whose influence has diminished since its high-water mark in 2019. Reintke won another term as co-chair, while Romanian MEP Ștefănuță won the second-place contest over Belgium’s Sara Matthieu and Sweden’s Isabella Lövin. Reintke cast the result as a mandate for “a very energetic two and a half years,” saying the pair would “do a lot of campaigning” on climate protection, social justice, democracy and the rule of law. Advertisement Advertisement But she also made clear that renewal would not mean a fundamental change of political course. “Obviously it’s a renewed leadership,” Reintke said. “But we are also going to continue the line on engaging and fighting in this house for everything that we can achieve in the next two and a half years.” Ștefănuță, meanwhile, presented the new leadership as an attempt to broaden the Greens’ appeal beyond their traditional environmental agenda, pointing to younger voters and bread-and-butter economic concerns. He said the group had chosen to “invest in dynamism” and a leadership that takes seriously concerns such as “the fact that the cost of living is very high” and problems with energy prices and economic stability. The pitch is a delicate balancing act: present a sense of renewal ahead of the 2029 European election without abandoning a long-held strategy. Reintke has led the Greens/EFA group since 2022. Ștefănuță has risen rapidly through its ranks since moving from Renew Europe in March 2023. Nine months later, the group elected him as one of its vice-presidents. He went on to become a vice-president of the European Parliament in July 2024. Advertisement Advertisement The Romanian gives the leadership a different geographical profile, something Reintke herself highlighted after the vote. She said Ștefănuță’s election reflected a desire for greater regional representation and would bring “a broader perspective on the different realities in Europe.” One of the leadership jobs was opened up by Bas Eickhout’s resignation as co-chair and as an MEP in May. Eickhout said at the time that he had had relationships that were inappropriate for his role and that he took responsibility for them. His departure removed one of the group’s most prominent politicians and triggered an unusually open contest for his replacement. The two new co-chairs now inherit the task of restoring some of the political weight the Greens enjoyed after the 2019 European election, when the group returned 74 MEPs and became the fourth-largest force in Parliament. Today, the Greens/EFA have 53 lawmakers and rank sixth. Reintke suggested that rebuilding those numbers could begin even before voters return to the polls. She said the group has “a strategy of growth” and wants to attract new MEPs, with discussions over possible enlargement expected in the coming months. Advertisement Advertisement

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/09/iran.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard claimed responsibility on Friday for setting an oil tanker ablaze in the Strait of Hormuz and threatened to pursue vessels it deems in violation beyond the strait and across the wider region, as maritime security agencies reported two further strikes on commercial ships in the Persian Gulf.The IRGC Navy said it targeted the engine room and propulsion system of the MV Sun Shine, a tanker belonging to the company Natwit, after the vessel attempted to use what it described as an unauthorised route through the strait's southern section. The attack caused a fire on board.In a statement, the IRGC warned that action against "violating" vessels would no longer be confined to the Strait of Hormuz and that any ship using what it deems unauthorised routes would be pursued and "punished" anywhere in the region.Companies it accuses of co-operating with the US would be sanctioned and all their vessels targeted, it added.The IRGC laid blame for the incidents in the strait on the US military, accusing Washington of interfering in the decisions of shipping and insurance companies and paying "large bribes" to induce compliance."Direct responsibility for these incidents and the escalation of tensions in maritime transport in the region lies with the aggressive US army," the statement said.Tehran's Friday prayer leader separately told his weekly sermon that the strait would remain closed until Iran's conditions were fully met.Hojjatoleslam Mohammad Javad Ali-Akbari said Iran had set out "seven conditions" and would decide its next steps once they were met, adding that military readiness had improved, weak points had been addressed, and Iran's strategy had shifted from defence to offence.Iran has said it controls the Strait of Hormuz and will not permit military forces from hostile countries in the area, vowing to respond "decisively" to any attempt to disrupt its management of the strait.Lanes clear, CENTCOM saysUS Central Command said on Friday it had cleared the strait's main shipping lanes, removed naval mines from principal transit routes, and declared them open to all vessels not in violation of US maritime sanctions against Iran.Thousands of commercial ships had passed through safely as a result, CENTCOM said.The competing claims came as the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre reported that an LPG carrier was struck by unknown projectiles on Friday morning, 13 nautical miles west of Al-Jazira in the United Arab Emirates, causing a major fire that was later brought under control.UKMTO had reported the previous day that an oil tanker north of Qatari waters was struck by several projectiles resulting in casualties, in the first such attack in six months.In a separate incident on Thursday, the maritime intelligence company Vanguard reported that a tanker had caught fire roughly 40 kilometres off Fujairah in the Gulf of Oman, identifying the vessel as probably the Dalkut, sailing under the Marshall Islands flag.At least 12 attacks, attempted attacks or harassment incidents targeting oil tankers and gas carriers were recorded in the strait between 28 September and 5 October, the highest weekly figure since the war began on 28 February, according to media reports.The Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil and gas shipments normally pass, has been effectively closed since the outbreak of the war, following Iranian missile and drone strikes on commercial vessels and a US Navy blockade of Iranian ports.The latest data indicate that oil exports from other countries in the region, excluding Iran, have returned to pre-war levels in recent days.

https://news.tuoitre.vn/young-vietnamese.text: Settings Saved news Your Comment Transaction History Logout Sunday, September 27, 2026, 10:15 GMT+7 Young Vietnamese chess players earn Grandmaster norms at Chess Olympiad Vietnam celebrated a double breakthrough on Saturday night as 20-year-old Nguyen Quoc Hy and 17-year-old Banh Gia Huy officially secured Grandmaster (GM) norms after 10 rounds at the 2026 Chess Olympiad, which runs from September 15 to 27 in Uzbekistan. A screenshot of Banh Gia Huy (L, 1st) and Nguyen Quoc Hy (L, 2nd), who secured Grandmaster norms at the 2026 Chess Olympiad. Facing a strong Norwegian side, Vietnam’s young players produced an impressive result, defeating their opponents 3-1. Beyond contributing to the team victory, both Hy and Huy completed the requirements for an international GM norm at the Olympiad. Hy has been one of Vietnam’s standout performers throughout the tournament, maintaining an unbeaten individual record from the opening rounds. After 10 demanding games in the open section, the 20-year-old recorded an impressive performance rating of 2,640. His route to the GM norm included five games against highly rated Grandmasters, against whom he remained undefeated, recording two wins and three draws. Before the 10th round, Hy had already defeated higher-rated Grandmasters Stamatis Kourkoulos-Arditis of Greece and Frode Urkedal of Norway. He also held three other strong Grandmasters to draws: Jan Malek of Poland, Yahli Sokolovsky of Israel, and Mahdi Gholami Orimi of Iran. His victory in the 10th round not only secured his first GM norm but also placed him among the relatively small group of Vietnamese players to achieve the feat at the highly competitive Chess Olympiad, following in the footsteps of established figures such as Le Quang Liem and Nguyen Duc Hoa. Nguyen Quoc Hy (in red) has impressed Vietnamese fans at the 2026 Chess Olympiad. Photo: Vietnam Chess Federation Like Hy, Huy maintained a strong level of performance, scoring 7.5 points from six wins, three draws, and one defeat to officially secure the norm. Vietnam’s players now have another opportunity to add to their individual achievements when they face Kazakhstan at 5:00 pm (Vietnam time) on Sunday. In particular, a victory for Dau Khuong Duy would see the 15-year-old player achieve the Grandmaster title. Meanwhile, Vietnam’s women continued their strong run, defeating Indonesia to move up to fifth place after 10 rounds of the Chess Olympiad. The Vietnamese women’s team will have a chance to challenge for an Olympiad medal if they defeat China in their final match of the tournament. Members of Vietnam's chess team left from Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City on September 13 for the world's biggest team chess event, hosted in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, with five male players competing in the open section and five female players in the women's section. The Olympiad features 11 rounds under the Swiss system. The event is expected to set a participation record, following the 2024 Olympiad in Budapest, which drew nearly 200 countries. https://www.indiatimes.com/trending/matc.text: Matchbox The Movie is an Apple TV action comedy that arrived on the platform on 9 October 2026 after a limited premiere at AMC Lincoln Square five days earlier.Directed by Sam Hargrave, the former stunt coordinator best known for the Extraction films, the picture runs 126 minutes and was written by David Coggeshall, with production involvement from Apple Studios, Skydance Media and Mattel Studios.John Cena leads as Sean Walker, a CIA operative who returns to his Ohio hometown for a funeral and finds his old friends pulled into an international mess involving a missing nuclear warhead. Jessica Biel plays Aimee, Sam Richardson is Crosby, Arturo Castro is Ted, and Teyonah Parris is Charmaine. Danai Gurira appears as Helen, Sean’s handler, with Corey Stoll as deputy director Mosier, Golshifteh Farahani as arms broker Robbie, and Bill Camp as the late mechanic Cal Smalley.The film draws on the Mattel toy line for its title and for the childhood garage where the core group once raced miniature cars, but the story quickly leaves the small-town setting for locations that include Bucharest and the area around Budapest.In the late 1990s the five friends spent afternoons in the back of Cal Smalley’s garage, pushing Matchbox cars around a model village he had built. Sean, Aimee, Crosby, Ted and Charmaine called themselves the Matchbox Gang. Sean had a particular soft spot for Aimee. She talked about a blue 1969 Super Camaro she wanted one day, and he bought the limited Matchbox version of it, intending to give it to her and say what he felt.Before he could, his father’s job took the family to Chicago. He left without the confession or the car.Nearly three decades later Sean works as a CIA operative under the Blackthorn programme. On one job he recovers a nuclear warhead from a warlord and passes it to a smuggler named Eastbrook, who is supposed to move it quietly toward allies in London. Helen, his handler and a colleague recruited around the same time, tells him to lie low for a while.News of Smalley’s death reaches him, so he goes home for the funeral. Aimee finds him in her uncle’s old workshop. She brings the rest of the group together for drinks. Ted teaches high-school science and has a husband and kids. Crosby works in construction and is married to Charmaine, who flies a news helicopter and reports traffic for a local station.Aimee works as a paramedic, drives an ambulance, and still races cars when she can. Sean tells them he is in international logistics. None of them buy it completely, but the night is easy until the drinks are spiked.They wake up bound in the cargo hold of a military transport. Mosier, who wants the top job at the agency, is convinced Sean stole the warhead after delivery. The friends are treated as accomplices. Sean gets them off the plane; they force Mosier out with a parachute and survive a rough landing. At that point the old group has no choice but to stay together if they want their ordinary lives back.Sean contacts Helen, expecting the person he has worked with for years to help clear the mess. She shows up, but her questions and the way she already knows details she should not know make him suspicious. He realises she arranged the theft herself. She needs Sean and the Matchbox Gang to look like terrorists so she can detonate the warhead on friendly soil, spark an international crisis, and then appear as the agent who stopped the rogue operative.The timing matters. NATO and Russian delegates are due to meet in Budapest for peace talks. A blast near that site would be blamed on Sean, and Helen’s path to a senior role would open.The group tracks the weapon to Bucharest, where an arms broker named Robbie has been asked to modify it. Robbie has history with Sean and does not trust him at first. Helen’s people arrive at the same building. Aimee and the others step in to pull Sean out. By then Helen has fitted the warhead with a proximity failsafe.The device tracks her distance from it. Once she moves roughly five kilometres away, the bomb is set to detonate on its own. She can leave the area while the explosion happens without her. That single modification forces the friends to stay close to the warhead for the rest of the chase. They load it into a vehicle and keep driving so the distance never grows too large, while Sean goes after the remote Helen carries.Mosier is still hunting them, unaware that Helen is the one who took the warhead. The friends use whatever skills they have: Aimee’s driving, Charmaine’s helicopter experience, Crosby’s knowledge of heavy equipment, Ted’s practical thinking. The chase moves toward Budapest because that is where Helen intends the device to go off.The group has to recover the remote and keep the warhead from crossing the failsafe threshold at the same time.Helen’s motive is straightforward career ambition. She and Sean were brought in together, but a past operation left her on a desk while he stayed in the field. Framing him and then stopping the attack she arranged would make Mosier look incompetent and position her for the promotion she wants. She works with a mercenary named Falko and uses the friends as cover. Because the failsafe is distance-based, simply locating the warhead is not enough.The group has to solve two problems at once: keep the device near them and get the remote away from her before she can create the required separation.In Bucharest, Robbie eventually helps once she understands Helen’s plan. She points them toward the convoy heading for the summit. The friends intercept it, but Helen reaches a helicopter. Sean manages to get aboard. During the fight the pilot is shot. The aircraft starts to go down. Sean ties Helen in place, takes the detonator, and jumps. The helicopter crashes with her still inside. She does not survive.With the remote in his hands he disarms the warhead before the distance trigger can fire. Mosier’s team arrives and takes the device into custody. Once Helen’s role is clear, Mosier accepts that Sean was framed and agrees to clear the names of the entire group. He also offers compensation for the kidnapping and the false charges that had been placed on them.The sequence is built around the practical problem the failsafe creates. The friends cannot park the warhead somewhere safe and wait. They have to stay in motion with it while Sean closes the gap on Helen. Aimee stays behind the wheel for long stretches. Charmaine’s familiarity with aircraft matters when the helicopter appears.The film treats the childhood Matchbox races as a loose parallel: the same group that once moved toy cars around a table now has to keep a real nuclear device from getting too far from its controller. After the pilot is hit, Sean restrains her, takes the remote, and leaves the aircraft. The helicopter goes down with her inside, and the film presents the death as final. There is no later scene suggesting she escaped or survived the impact.With the detonator recovered, Sean disables the proximity mechanism and the warhead is secured. It does not explode. Mosier’s team takes possession of it, and the charges against Sean and the friends are dropped. The device returns to CIA control, which is where it was supposed to have been after the original recovery mission.The ending also closes the personal threads. At Crosby and Charmaine’s farewell gathering, Aimee finds the old blue Matchbox Camaro on the dashboard of her ambulance. Sean arrives driving the full-size 1969 Camaro he once planned to give her. He tells her he has kept the feelings he never managed to say when they were teenagers. They kiss. Crosby, who has spent years avoiding flights, decides to move with Charmaine to Seattle for the job she has been offered.Ted goes back to his husband and children. Sean, who spent most of the film insisting he works alone, stays with Aimee. The warhead is safe, the frame-up is exposed, and the group that started as kids racing cars in a garage ends the story with most of its members still together.The film does not leave open questions about the bomb or about Helen. Once the remote is in Sean’s possession and she is no longer able to create the required distance, the immediate threat ends. Mosier’s change of position once the evidence is clear allows the friends to step out of the terrorism accusations that had followed them.The last image returns to the Camaro and the unfinished childhood promise, rather than to any further agency business.Matchbox The Movie is available to stream on Apple TV. It was released globally on 9 October 2026.
